reviews.t: A Great Way To Paint With-In The Lines
reviews.x: This product is specific to masking of hobby models or other small areas.  You typically apply the product with a brush to area on the model that needs to be painted with a detail or design.  When the solution drys you take an hobby knife and make an outline cut and pull away any excess material. (Lets say you wish to paint a square - you would make cuts in the material in the shape of a square - peel the square away leaving an area to be painted)  It leaves a mask - almost like a stencil or pai

I started using this product as soon as I found it. It goes on quickly and easily. You just paint it on the area you want to protect from being painted and paint over it. Once the paint is dry, just peel it off.  I have used a couple of other masking products and I cannot really tell a difference between them. They all seem to work about the same. Since I use other products (MicroSet and MicroSol) I guess there is a bit of brand loyalty going on for me. Having said that, though, I would still us

reviews.t: I love Microscale products but this is not one of them
reviews.x: This masking product does brush on easily and does work on the areas you want to protect, but it dries very stiff and is difficult to trim without it wanting to lift off from the plastic. And it is difficult to tell if an area is successfully covered since it has just a slight blue tint to it. When dry, I can't tell sometimes if it is still on the area I want to protect. If this product wants to be perfect it needs to be more flexible, stick to plastics a little more, and have more pigment in it

reviews.t: Great product. Use once and you should be hooked.
reviews.x: I really love this stuff. Just a few tips. First, clean the area. I use accelerator and this stuff may not stick to it very well. You might want to use a small filter cloth to clean with alcohol first. Gun cleaning patches work wonder by the way! Secondly, use multiple coats. Two reasons. You will get full coverage this way. If you have not cleaned the area on clear plastic you will not get full coverage. Multiple coats will eventually fill the gaps and provide great coverage. Also, thicker coat

Works pretty good. I first tried this on a 1:144 scale airplane with a tri-color camouflage scheme, and found it saved time versus cutting a masks from tape.  I had two problems: when applying over a painted surface the liquid mask 'clumped up' and contracted as it dried requiring repeated applications to cover an area; and, perhaps due to the small scale, removing the mask was tedious--it wouldn't peel and had to be stripped off using masking tape.

Apply spots of a dark brown color to the model.  4. using a sponge with a little bit of this product dab it over the model in random locations.  Places in which there would likely be chipping. Takes a little trial and error, but this stuff works as advertised.  It would be nice if this worked with water based acrylics, but it is a pleasure to work with.

reviews.t: This Stuff is an Answer to Prayer
reviews.x: I can not sing enough praised about any MicroScale product, especially their liquid mask.  In the old days, you had to cut miles of masking tap and wrestle with applying it.  Now you just brush this stuff on, let it cure, apply paint, let it dry then remove.

This product actually was delivered the day after I ordered it.  My husband uses it when making his models and assures me it is geat quality and makes his hobby easier.  He was very happy to be able to order it online.  He says it is a very good product.

reviews.t: mixed expereince, but I don't know anything does the same job tha twould be any different.

Everything I buy from tho company has been good. The micro mask does its job. I feel it may be a little thin going on, but it covers well and removes easily. I used it as a paint mask for camo on a model plane I was building. The end result was very nice. This was my first time painting on camo so I would ask all of my fellow modelers to go easy on me. Thanks

As one always on the lookout for better ways to model "chips" in paint, I chose this product with the intention of applying by sponge, and removing with a Q-Tip or masking tape. Because of the small scale of my project, I used a fine sponge (the type that comes on foam paint brushes). This necessitated that the quantity of Micro Mask be very thin in depth and tiny in area covered. reviews.t: This may be good for very limited uses
reviews.x: This may be good for very limited uses, but I don't have any of those uses to test. The main issue is that it is for oil-based paint only, which has limited miniature/model applications. While the bottle didn't specify what surfaces it can safely coat, I have tried a few. It bonded to acrylic and alcohol base paint, unable to be removed. Also bonds to primer and the enamel I tested. Makes it mostly useless except for specific applications.  Unfortunately, the product description didn't mention w

reviews.t: Wish it would work with water base paints
reviews.x: Works well but does take some practice to get it right. I suggest you practice on scrap before attempting to use on your project. Also it says not to use with water based paints and I use a lot of acrylics so this does limit its use.
This stuff is magic for masking small spaces, especially if they have raised edges surrounding.  However, caution is warranted for larger surfaces.  Treat those with masking tape.

reviews.t: Cannot be used with water-based paints
reviews.x: It says on the bottle that it cannot be used with water-based paints (vallejo, citadel, model master acrylic).  I wish I had known this before I bought it.

reviews.t: Good product; as good as you ar at applying it.
reviews.x: Masking property works great, but it's like painting on a mask by hand; so if you aren't good at painting with a brush...this will challenge you.
This is junk! I used it hard to get off. Does not mask very good. I would not.recommand this product.  Back to using maskinh tape.
Stuff is lousy. Didn't work at all. Didn't block paint at all. Guess you have to really slather it on for it to be effective.

reviews.t: Doesn't adhere well to clear parts, Works well if you don't expect too much
reviews.x: The most obvious use for this mask I could think of was masking clear windows on airplane canopies, but the mask doesn't really like to stick to the clear parts that well.  I expected it to be much more aggressive so that I could cut intricate details, but fine lines of this mask just lift off (Think the thin braces between panes on an X-1 or a B-52.  I ended up painting those by hand).  I did manage to make this work on more simple shapes, but it is still pretty fragile. You could probably mix

I have never used a liquid mask on my models and decided to try this on a NASCAR kit that I built this month. I followed directions and used as suggested. The results amazed me. I was skeptical at first because the film dries and is kind of hard to see. It worked great and I plane to use this on the rest of the kits I build. I did get one or 2 "bleed" spots but that was my fault for not applying it all the way to the line

Does what it says it does, but its trickier than you might think.  I wish it was slightly more opaque, or a brighter tint, as it's quite easy to miss pieces of it, especially over dark colors.  If you wait too long to make the cuts, it gets brittle and the edges can lift and paint can get under them.  For very small details I had better results with a fine brush.  Good product, but there is a learning curve.

reviews.t: Great product, but similar can be had in larger quantities, for less money.
reviews.x: The product is essentially everything it says, but save yourself some money and buy a large bottle of liquid masking at a store like Michaels using a 40% off coupon like they always have available.  The product is fine, the cost is where you'll question the decision to purchase this over a larger sized bottle at a craft store, is all.

USE ONLY IN CONJUNCTION WITH ENAMEL PAINTS!  ACRYLIC AND WATER BASED PAINTS WILL INTERFERE WITH THIS MASKING FLUID!  For a fluid that won't have that issue, Humbrol masking fluid will be a better choice, but for what it's worth, Micro Mask is as superb as all other products of its brand, and a must-have for any model workbench.

Once you get used to how to apply product (I multi coat) it works really well. I use it for windows and lenses on WW2 vehicles. I do not use it to mask decals, as I ran into problems with adherence of paint to product. I think it was my bad though. You will have to experiment with it. Overall, it does a fine job of masking.

claims.text: Reviewers frequently praise the product as a quick, easy, and effective way to mask small areas on models, saving time versus cutting tape.
Several reviewers note it takes practice and trial and error to get right, recommending testing on scrap first.
Some reviewers report problems with application and drying, such as clumping over painted surfaces, drying stiff and lifting when trimmed, or needing multiple coats.
Multiple reviewers mention it is not compatible with water-based acrylic paints, limiting its use for those who work with acrylics.
Reviewers describe using it successfully for weathering and chipping effects on models.
